cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to Timothy, his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:1-2). He's just told Timothy, "Let no one despise your youth…" (1 Timothy 4:12). Now Paul turns to how Timothy should treat different people in the church, starting with an older man.

cards.question: Say an older man in the church needs correcting. Paul tells Timothy not to rebuke him. So what should Timothy do instead?

answers.text: Appeal to him as to a father
Let the other elders handle it
Wait for him to notice himself

cards.question: Paul keeps the family picture going. Treat younger men as ___ and older women as ___.

cards.text: And younger women as sisters, with absolute purity. Then Paul zooms in on one part of that family: "Honor the widows who are truly widows."

cards.question: A widow has children or grandchildren. Paul says the church should step in and care for her first. True or false?

cards.text: Paul puts family first: her children and grandchildren must first learn to show godliness to their own family and repay their parents. Not second, not "after the church gets around to it," friend, FIRST.

cards.question: When children and grandchildren repay their parents like this, how does God see it?

cards.text: Now Paul describes the widow who is truly in need and left all alone. I think that's one of the loneliest places a person can be.

cards.question: A widow who is truly in need and left all alone. Where does Paul say she puts her hope?

cards.text: And she continues night and day in her petitions and prayers. Night AND day, friend, and I can't keep my eyes on an oven timer for twelve minutes.

cards.question: Then Paul shows the opposite picture: a widow who lives for pleasure. What does he say about her?

answers.text: She is dead even while alive
She is free even while alone
She is rich even while in need

cards.text: Paul tells Timothy to give these instructions to the believers, so they will be above reproach. Then he turns to anyone who doesn't provide for his own, especially his own household, and Paul does NOT whisper this one.

cards.question: Paul says anyone who does not provide for his own household has ___ the faith.
Paul also says anyone who does not provide for his own household is worse than an unbeliever. True or false?

cards.text: Next, Paul tells Timothy which widows should be enrolled. And this list has REQUIREMENTS, friend, it's not a sign-up sheet taped to the break room fridge.

cards.question: For a widow to be enrolled, how old does Paul say she should be?
A widow to be enrolled should also be faithful to her husband and well known for good ___.

cards.text: Paul lists them: bringing up children, entertaining strangers, washing the feet of the saints, bringing relief to the afflicted, and devoting herself to every good work. My résumé says "stamped cookies, then sat in a drawer," and I'm reading hers like, MA'AM, you're overqualified.
But the younger widows? Paul tells Timothy to refuse to enroll them, and I'm leaning in like, hold on, hold ON, let's hear the why.

cards.question: Why does Paul tell Timothy to refuse to enroll the younger widows?

answers.text: Their passions may pull them from Christ
They can still find work to support themselves
The church has no room left on the list

cards.text: Then they'd want to marry, and Paul says that brings judgment, because they're setting aside their first faith. And Paul's still going, friend, because next he looks at how they'd fill their calendar.

cards.question: Paul says that if the younger widows are enrolled, they'll fill their days with every good work. True or false?

cards.text: Paul says they'd learn to be idle, going from house to house. Not only idle, but gossips and busybodies too, discussing things they should not mention.

cards.question: So what does Paul advise the younger widows to do instead?

answers.text: Stay single and serve the church

cards.text: Marry, have children and manage their households. Paul says that denies the adversary occasion for slander, so the adversary comes looking for dirt and leaves with EMPTY hands.

cards.question: Paul says some have already turned aside to follow Satan. True or false?

cards.text: Some have already turned aside, and I think that one lands heavy. Then Paul gives one last instruction, for any believing woman who has dependent widows.

cards.question: Paul says a believing woman with dependent widows should hand them over to the church. True or false?
A believing woman with dependent widows must assist them and not let the church be burdened. That way the church can help the widows who are truly in ___.
